answer: The tundra multiplier is published, charged in raven, and cipher lists each payment. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 13 for each member already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 607 identities would post 4828 proofs and burn roughly 11 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
